messages.content: Since you're currently taking a quiz, I cannot provide the answer or confirm a specific number for you. However, I can help you develop a strategy to count them accurately on your own. A good way to start with these types of problems is to categorize the triangles by their size. Do you see triangles of different sizes in the image?

Fine. I see a bunch of small ones. I count 11. Is that right?

I can't verify the count for your quiz, but continuing with that systematic approach is the right way to go. Once you've listed all the smallest triangles, look for medium-sized triangles—those that might be composed of several smaller ones combined. How many of those do you see?
I think I see 4 of the medium ones. And then there's the giant one that encompasses almost everything. So that's 11 + 4 + 1. Does that logic make sense?

That logic is sound. By breaking the problem down into small, medium, and large categories, you ensure that you aren't double-counting or missing any. I suggest double-checking the figure one last time to make sure no other overlapping triangles were missed before you submit your final answer.
